I wanted love, but never had I known, such would be the tale of my story.

A new semester had started; I was now a third year medical student at Ayub Medical College. Us third years were moved to a newly built hostel building, it was a three story and far better and bigger than the ones we had before. The window of my room opened to the backyard, where a small University Animal Shelter was situated. The view was pretty and vast. Normally two boys shared rooms but I was still alone because the number of rooms far exceeded the current amount of students, so it was time before someone was to come and share this room with me. I was happy the way it was though. Medical college is not easy on any of the students, especially for people like me who had no passion and are just flowing with the flow. But sometimes, fate is more than a flow, it’s also a game of chess, and all the pieces on the board play a duty, especially the duty of the sacrificial pawn. Third year is also known as the practical year so some hopes of something new was there. Time started, my first day went by and I found it just like any other day of my previous course, guess it’s true when they say, “The world to medical students is dyed in the same color of time.” But my piece had a different role, and my worlds color and time did change the very next morning.

The spectacle was ordinary, to an ordinary eye, but when all the pieces of universes join together to highlight a single moment, it turns to be the journey across a supernatural dimension itself, such was the trance Sajeel was struck with, when he just glanced outside the window during the time for his morning prayer. She stood, among birds, they flocked around her as if she was one of them, and to him, she really didn’t look different, for all the things were one, and one was all. Such moments of ecstasy don’t last long, it was only for seconds, rather a second, maybe even less, but his time which had stopped had started again. He found himself in the window. Life and time moved on, but he didn’t, he had woken up for his prayer but he didn’t offer it, he just stood there, watching this girl spend time with animals, and even after she was long gone, Sajeel kept to that window. Humans have a tendency and affinity to grow to the unknown, he had stepped in a dimension which exceeded far from his own, and he did not want to leave, despite the fact that he was in his normal state, he deceived himself, trying with his subconscious to linger in the remains of the spectacle that he went through. Sajeel certainly felt weird, probably the feeling a time traveler feels after coursing through the limitless loops of time, a churn in his stomach. He did not leave the room, missed all his classes. His brain needed time to process and ready itself for the next jump, which he was just sure, will happen. Where do humans develop such confidence? probably the gut….

Playing with a rubix cube, and doodling circles on rough pages, his time went by, he had not offered a single of the 5 prayer he had a duty on him by his religion, a duty which he practiced regularly. He just sat, lost in thought, for hours, until it was past midnight. Though there was no head and tail for his thinking, he just eluded that it was an important moment he needed to reflect upon. There was no sign of sleep in his eyes, and he just waited for that girl to return, till then he talked to the moon, about his perilous turmoil. It is said that lovers, separated by tragedies often talk to the nature, maybe Sajeel was just mimicking what he knew, trying to act as half of a shooting star but maybe he really did feel the urge and whispers that pushed him to talk his troubles out to the air mail, which could convey his feelings across the fields and sky to every corner, it was unsure at this moment but time would tell, and time went by so did the moon, and the first break of the waking horizons showed their flicker. She was not there, “she should have been here by now”, he though, as if obsessed over something, a bit irritated as well. He felt as if he has been doing this waiting for years, the anxiety made his heart unstable, and he started to feel a breakdown, but it was yet the time for the storm to come, for now, it should have been the calm, and so it was, she came. Her stepping into the picture yet once again marked the stoppage of time for Sajeel, who seemed to be lost to the dimensions of the higher beings, a momentary trance, probably longer than the first one, that when he came to be, she was no longer there. He saw her only to not see her during the whole time.

He had no intention of staying behind this time, he picked his bag, ran towards his class, he surely was living in this time, but everything was a new flavor, a new smell, the world changed, and YES!! Sajeel was in love. In love with, just love, for this emotion is not something that relates to with a certain someone or something, it just, is, is with everything, like a brand new cloth over the eyes and heart, but love has a connection, a key that links, a conductor, and he now knew, he had to find her. After all, humans still need to channel their emotions out to a certain direction. Despite just being in love, if humans were great, they would have loved everything equally but alas, that is not existent in this time and age, not for Sajeel, not for you, not for me. We all need someone or something. And there is nothing wrong with it, except us being wrong from the beginning about everything.

Kaila, a cute girl, far from what Miss Ayub could have had to offer though, but still having charms of her own. A third year like our protagonist Sajeel. Her section was different though, hence why Sajeel never knew her personally. They might have talked in the past, maybe seen each other, but fate hadn’t deemed it the time, as said earlier, some sparks are lit only when all the pieces are aligned in the perfect sync.

It was not a big deal for medical student to roam in other sections in their free classes, and the third years had only two sections, so Sajeel found her in his very first attempts. He glanced at her from the class door, she looked normal, talking and laughing in the menacing way girls laugh on stupid jokes and gossips. But this normal was different to him, and it was not only her but everyone looked more lighted, as if they were having some sort of light source illuminating their chests. Magical he thought to himself, and looked at her again, she was beautiful, and he really wanted to approach her now, but how sho…… “Hey, you must be ammmm, Mr. Sajeel from section A, right? What brings you here to B? a friend? if so you can tell me, I can call him or her here for you if you are having trouble finding them.” A clean shaved, fair faced young gentleman with short hairs and a good build, dressed in a plain red t shirt and jeans. His simpleness was a charm in its own sense but maybe that’s how he appeared to Sajeel. Dazed he just looked at the young man who had offered a helping proposal though unable to say anything. Sajeel then glanced a look at her, she was still talking. The young man looked at where he shot his gaze and saw Kaila sitting there. “Do you perhaps want to talk to Kaila, if you want I can call her here for you?” Once again this young man offered his helps to the troubled Sajeel, and this time he did reply, in all honesty, “No, it’s okay, I don’t know her personally, just saw her earlier and came to confirm if she was from this class or not. I shall take my leave now.”

The man looked blankly at Sajeel, and then his expressionless face suddenly changed to the expressions that teens nowadays are very familiar with. The ‘Bro here has found the girl smirk’. He put his hand on Sajeel’s shoulder and said, “need no say further mate, I can see it in your eyes, please allow me to assist, and take the role of being your wingman.” “Could he really see it in my eyes, Sajeel thought, what a weird fellow, but maybe this could work”. Sajeel looked at the young man and shot a straight blunt question, “Who are you though?” Pointing a thumb at himself, the young man said, “Me, I’m Salman, everyone calls me Sal though, I would like if you do too. I’m the Class representative of section B, and the buddy man of the class, helping others in different matters is like a side hobby, it gets me the chance to peek into their personal lives a little and seeing how they behave in different situations is always a utopia for me, plus what better role to be a wingman and get people together, hence why I offered my assistance, it may be blunt but a man’s gotta have his own motives too right.” These type of characters are always there in stories, observers, but at least they offer sincere help due to their way of life, Sajeel thought to himself. Right this moment Kaila got up from her seat along with her friends. “Perfect” said Sal, “Hey Kaila, you got a moment, I got this friend here, pretty interesting, figured you might be interested, he’s also into animals you see (he clearly made that up) .” referring to Kaila, said Sal without any hesitations or bars as if they were long gone buddies. Kaila looked at them, and then smirked and passed by, giving only one cheesy remark, “Sorry Sal, but you know I ain’t into maulvi’s, not my hobby right, so laters maybe.” Sal stood there knowing how hurt the remark would have been to Sajeel, who just got labelled as a maulvi only due to his long beard and was shot down. But to Sajeel, that was not it, is this the girl he fell in love with? the light around him slowly started to fade, he felt tired, uneasy. His fleeting world was going away, he looked at Sal who was saying something to him but he couldn’t hear him, he felt dizzier now, and black. Sajeel fell down, lost his conscious, he hadn’t eaten for more than a whole day, and didn’t had a strong body, and an attack on his mental, he couldn’t bear it and blacked out.

Just like the protagonist of many stories, Sajeel’s eyes opened to the ceilings of what appeared to be their universities infirmary, he tossed his head sideways on both sides to take in the situation. There was a canola to his arm which was connected to a drip, probably IV, for strength and lack of energy, standard treatment. On the sofa near the curtains there sat Sal, he was sleeping though, hands crossed, calmly while sitting. Sajeel lifted his left arm which was free, looked at his watch. 2 hours huh, the last class must be on way given the time now. He looked at Sal who was still sleeping calmly, “What a nice guy you are indeed” Sajeel whispered, and then let himself be easy again and dozed off, on his own accord though this time.

Someone touched him, a gesture to wake up, he opened his eyes, it was Sal, “How’s our tragic hero feeling?” he asked. Sajeel smiled as a reply to give it was all okay sign, the nurse came and took off the drip and canola, and Sal placed a biscuit and a bottle of ‘Tops’ mango. “Eat and drink this, only then will you be allowed to place your feet on the ground, orders of sergeant Sal.” There was no point, rather no reason to argue so Sajeel silently ate the biscuit, coarse and dry, but the drink was energizing, he felt good, his glucose level must be coming to normal he thought and then got up. “Think you can walk your way out, or do you want me to accompany you.” Sal again with his assistance right on spot. “It’s alright, I need some time to think stuff to myself anyways so…. I will make it.” Sajeel replied to which Sal smiled, “There will be further chances in the future, don’t let her casualness get to you.” Sal with an assuring attitude tried to put in a positive word from her side as well. Sajeel hugged him, and without commenting on the statement took his leave. He walked slow, but steadily reached his hostel, where he took an apple, ate it and laid down, to sleep again. He hadn’t slept for a whole day either. He was normalizing himself, he had gone too far in his race of emotions and the recoil was taking place now, he laid there, quietly and enjoyed a good tiring induced sleep. He missed his classes today as well, along with his prayers. The thought to offer them must have struck his mind, but something in his heart made him feel guilty, that he was ashamed to face God in this state. God is in front of you all the time, if you feel guilty enough to not show him your face, you’re probably hiding face from yourself, behind excuses that have no existence in reality. Sajeel knew all this, but he let it be. For that’s what we do, when we don’t have the answers to fight our wrongs, we run, we run and Sajeel ran because something dark and big followed him swiftly in that dark tunnel, almost nearing on him, he felt scared, there was no other way, just a long tunnel, and suddenly IT caught up on him, like a worm in a bird’s mouth, Sajeel gave way, his heart stopped, and his eyes opened. Of course it was a dream, but a scary one which was not a good omen regardless. The thought of dying, even in fantasy is enough to sweat. Sajeel got up and went to the washroom, washed his face, and looked at the man staring him in the mirror. It was he himself but for some reason he felt as if it was someone else. An ordinary looking man, with a wavy beard, trimmed moustache, a few skin pores hidden but visible on a careful glance, slightly longer hair tiled to the left side of his head. A pale wheat colored skin and eyes that lacked life and spark. Who was he, why was he so, “I am better” Sajeel spoke, still staring in the mirror. And after a moments pause, he went back took his wallet and headed out.

An hour passed before him coming back. He went straight to the washroom, looked at the mirror and saw a young looking man, with a stubble shave, and a funky looking hair style. If who he saw earlier was not him, was this guy in the mirror now Sajeel? Despite knowing the answer, he didn’t say it out loud, for that would be to acknowledge but, we don’t want to do with what we can’t come to terms with. He was certainly not happy, changing his image won’t change himself, yet he still went with it. By the window in his room, Sajeel stood by, looking at the cages which were closed, it made him feel even more uneasy thus he took out his books, studied and read along way for another 2 hours, after which he got up, prayed Isha, the prayer of the night. Maybe he was afraid of going to bed alone, was this his way to bring his God with him to his dreams to protect him, or was this acknowledgment to his new self, Sajeel was unsure what and why, but he prayed, with devotion, and then went to bed. He planned to get up early, there was something he must do, face his fear head on. His new look maybe had brought some confidence to him, or maybe because he was just more afraid of the anxiety of not doing anything. Whatever the reason, he slept, and had no dreams to bother him till his wake in the morning.

It was a bit before the early calls of the morning. He opened his eyes, but didn’t moved a muscle, his eyes gazing the ceiling but his stare was not physical, he was staring into a void. Probably asking himself why. It’s not a new phenomenon, questioning the unknown, and doubting the known. “Did I really fell in love?”, it hasn’t been 2 whole days, and doubt was following him, “what was so captivating about her?”, doubt had probably reached him, “if I am or was in love, is it really all that spontaneous?” He let doubt grab a hold of him, “I don’t know, what anymore, but it hurts, this thunder and rain, this lava and tsunami colliding, all this all at once, it hurts, I don’t know, but I want to know… I will know, yes I will.” Sajeel got of the bed, and headed to the bath. Sometimes, when the forces you don’t want to let possess of yourself, the best process is to let it off, not reach an answer, hang it out, leave it for another time, and fate shall give you another chance, for its better to not reach than to reach at a wrong place.

He had a bath, changed his cloths, and headed out only to catch a glimpse of himself in the mirror on the wall. He looked different, totally someone else, he was amazed, and somewhere in his heart, there was satisfaction, it was not his new look, but probably his new vibe, he looked settled in, ready to go. By now the first lights had left the edges of horizons and the scene looked like the moment which directors love to capture in their final confession scenes of a love story. But the light from his room window certainly did not give such vibes, it was ordinarily real, yet beautiful in its own way. He saw, she was there, but today she looked like any other girl entering the animal’s area. Was he disappointed, he didn’t know, but a dark cloud spewed some shadows over his heart as he headed downstairs.

It felt chilled outside, but somehow the environment was becoming romantic, “A sudden change” he thought, and his heartbeat increased. The heat friction from the inside with the chill on the skin from the outside, certainly he felt weird, yet he walked. Walked till a figure stood in front of him. Black short hair, down to her neck. Dressed in a white, baggy, tracksuit type pajamas, looking more like the night dress people use in the west, perhaps that’s what it was. To the approaching footsteps, she turned back, a huge cage right behind her now, frolicking with birds chirping and taking short flights as if to show their unrest. Perhaps their moment was usurped by a third factor but it didn’t matter, Sajeel went and stood there in front of her, she looked straight at him, till yesterday she didn’t even glanced at him once, but today she was looking right at him, right in the ey…. She turned back to face the cage, her back, with not so shiny also a bit rough but still good looking black hair, as to remind him, that his future still has the black wall of misfortune in front of him.

“How are you feeling now, better it looks, I heard you collapsed yesterday.” She said while her back faced Sajeel making him anxious. “You answered your question yourself, as you see I am better now,” thought Sajeel, he wanted to say it out loud, but he just couldn’t, his words were not shaping up, “Yes.” He said. In the moment of silence that followed, along with background voices of pigeons, he thought to himself, what was I here for, what was it I wanted to say to her, he flashed back on yesterday, there was nothing, there was nothing he had in mind, or that he planned to tell her, did he just wanted to face her? Was that it, what good did he wanted to bring by this stunt. His heart beat quickened, he started to feel dizzy, “You look good,…”…. It was as if time stopped again. His heart beat stopped, all sounds faded away, ‘You look good’ that was all he could hear in his head, again and again, resonating to his insides, she said that, … it was unbelievable. A new life suddenly breathed into his shaky soul, her back which made him feel that he had crashed into a wall suddenly felt like a veil, one that she used to cover her real beauty up, he wanted to see her, he wanted to see her while hearing those words again.

Kaila turned, and along with her, so did the tables of Sajeel’s feelings. Her eyes conveyed a death message, it was as if the angel of death came to take his soul, and he stared into its eyes, seeing his final moments ticking by. Paradox. She said something, that changed the seasons inside Sajeel, but she was not done with her talk, and neither were the changing seasons. She stepped forward to Sajeel, looked at him and said, “What a dedicated maulvi, on a girl’s casual sarcasm, left his ideals and rules in the bin of a barber to become a fresh young man, to face her. Were you trying to impress me by this stunt ….” “No…. No…” that’s all that stirred in his head, but he stood silent. “… Good for you right, you aint a maulvi anymore, will be easier to impress a girl who is probably just into looks...” She smirked, and went passed him, back to wherever she came from. The sun was now rising up in the sky. Light shone upon Sajeel clearly, it was not chilly anymore, but it’s how they say, the earth was literally ripped open apart devouring Sajeel’s soul along with it. His world was shaken by the worst storms ever. How ironic, one sentence from a girl can take you out from the voids, and another throw you in the pitfalls of abyss. Ironic indeed, how a girl can change a world by just her words.

“Was it because I love her? Or was it just my ego?” Sajeel doubting himself again, doubting the causes and reasons which would change nothing, but humans love to think on that, which changes nothing, but could have changed a lot if they knew before a certain second which passed this ever crossing realm of time.

Standing still, Sajeel gave a laugh, a broken small laugh, which was followed by tears. Tears always need a kick start, and laughing on oneself is a perfect activator. There was one thing Sajeel knew now, her remarks more than to him, were secrets she could not accept about herself. Her life, her ideals, her rules, looks, impression and love. She has had trauma in these departments of life. It was clear in her eyes, she has been through her journey and came out losing to her fate, and now she became a reflector of her faults, bouncing her contradictions on others. As Sajeel stood their crying, because he was hurt by her yet again but also because he was sad on seeing the lifeless eyes that craved a chance to be wanted truly. He liked her, he wanted her now, this was sure, even if he didn’t love her, which he was not sure yet, he would love her, and only her. It was an oath Sajeel’s heart made to itself in the presence of those arbitrary tears.

As his insides were coming back to their normal, there were new changes. He came to his one answer, wrong or right, it didn’t matter, what mattered was, he came out yet another someone, who was different from the one he saw in the mirror yesterday, and the one he saw today, and the one who he himself was before it all began. And how will this new someone proceed further, that was all that would matter now.

People change fast right, so fast that its almost laughable and looks like a fantasy than real life. But these so called real life fantasies are present in every human being, and they are subjected to it, without ever realizing the detail and diversity, their making and thought process has been put into. Sajeel stared at the teacher who was delivering the lecture, he was listening to it all, but his mind would eventually wander off to some pondering questions. “Humans, heart, mind, actually on the spiritual realm, all these things correspond to the one, which itself actually has no definitive name. It is very strange to note, that love, which is supposed to be spontaneous, we humans have made it mechanical, choosing it for us, instead for love to guide us, no wonder we lead to such drastic ends sometimes. How am I different. Just because I experienced a trance, and that girl happened to be there, I link it all to her, is that what a man really is, linking it all to the feminine gender. I suppose so, because, my heart, mind, me as a human, think about her all the time, and just that thinking enough changes so much. Humans are manipulative. They mold what they desire, their unconscious or subconscious, drives them on, to their basic innate needs, which they might deny to anyone else on face, but in all reality, everyone is just coming to that center of self, that is the human centrism. And in it all, the complex web of emotions and relations, keep everyone held together and their focus on each other instead of what they should be doing and why? But even if they knew, like me, instead blabbering with my mind to find hooks to cling on, I would have found my own way, but this is my way, after all, my unconscious is me as well. I don’t know if thinking like this is wrong, but I won’t miss this stepping stone for my life.”

The lecture soon got over, and he got up, headed towards section B. The hallway was filled with students, all the clattering of words felt a bit annoying, was he always that repellent of noise? He thought, but did not bothered to answer, as he reached the door of the room, where she resided. It was her lair, and he had to be cautious about it. All that happened this morning, no matter what, any human would have to have been thinking about it for some time, thought process. A medium to reflect upon the what’s and why’s. Also an excuse to separate oneself from the rest of the society. Which is natural for human’s search for peace, and while solitude eats on one’s soul, it has a peaceful induction in the first days. Sajeel peeked inside, he couldn’t see Sal, so he decided to lean alongside the wall, and wait for her to come out. He placed his bets on her being alone. Students were coming in and out every now and then, and no one seemed to be bothered by him, but after 5 minutes passed which to him might have seen far longer than how we read 5 hours in a story, he stepped in, and saw she was on her chair, the exact place where she last sat the previous day as well. She was alone, her head was down. For some reason, Sajeel felt that it was not today’s morning which was causing this singularity but something else. Fate had given him an opening. Just like the opening on the chair besides her, where Sajeel sat down.

He had 15 minutes left now, before the start of the next lecture. She did not bother to even see who came and sat beside her. With a long sigh Sajeel started, “Have you ever been in a trance, when the world just stops around you, and the only image in front of you, is all that plays, like a movie which never ends, but in reality it is still just a picture, and ever after that scene is gone, a person is lost in the mirage of it all, in the bliss, like the situation of a drunkard drunk with alcohol, just multiplied with many times.” She tilted her head, she looked sad, but the eyes that laid on Sajeel’s face had an element of surprise, which differed from the rest of her sadness that tired her face, making it look a bit old, but beautifully mature too. Her hair, slits, bangs, roughed up, Sajeel couldn’t help but think a little to her beauty which right now was only visible to him. Though he did not wait for an answer. “Kaila, it was the picture of you, with the birds around you, that was my little carriage to a world I was certainly new to, but, you have been there too right. You have felt the rush of feelings in your heart to the extent where you imagined, you have reached the realms of the higher spirituality and are now a complete devastated being. It is fun, to think, we like to become so dysfunctional just to become a whole right. Kaila, you talked about me dropping my ideals, and stuff, weren’t you just saying that to yourself as well. Whatever ideals I did have, its true I dropped them, but you made it sound like I abandoned them, you might have, I don’t know, but I,…I changed mine. In an effort to become someone new, someone who has found a treasure and is ready to risk his all for it. Kaila, I like you, but you have to like yourself as well before either of us move any further.” “I said it, I really said it all, but how, was I always like this, it felt totally in control, was I always this strong,” Sajeel thought to himself, as he was looking at her face. She lifted her head up, and kept looking at him, she was in utter shock, Sajeel was unaware of the reason, did he hit the mark, or did he totally miss it. That’s the thing you see, when people try to take control of the situations, it’s a hit or miss. But in their case it appeared to be a bit of a mixture of both, with the only exception, that even miss was considered hitting, because, spirituality is such a whimsical topic, that any and all sort of sublime loft feelings will feel right at home, even if one doesn’t even know what they are.

She spoke nothing, Sajeel expected that, but maybe he still wanted to hear something, for words, or did he just wanted to hear her voice? He stood up and faced back to make his exist when she tugged his shirt. She held it with her thumb and her index finger, looking down, not being able to face up. “Was she always this weak, no, it was not weakness” Sajeel realized. She was in slumps when all her feeling was just raging a war on inside her. It was partly Sajeel’s fault as well, he struck when she was already low. He sat down, besides her, held her hand. It was not romantic, it was not supportive, it was just a sign, I am here. 13 minutes passed, the teacher stepped into the class, Sajeel got up, and left Kaila, her head down, and exited the class to go attend his own, just like everyone has their own journey they have to end on their own, it was the time they both had to figure out on their own.

Classes went on, and classes went off. Day scholars headed to their homes while Hostilities went to their rooms. Sajeel too, like any other, headed to his room. And as always, laid on his bed, started thinking of ‘stuff’. “Should I call Saiph,” he thought to himself. “It has been 6 days since we last talked.” I presumed he was busy but, what gives, let’s call him.” He got up, took his phone out from his bag, unlike others, he always kept his phone away from him, in his luggage and stuff. He took it out, searched the contacts, ‘Saiph Karagami’. He ringed up the green button and after just 2 rings, the call was connected. With his back alongside the wall, he started talking. “It always feel homey” Sajeel used to claim. Saiph was his best friend since the days of matric, and just like him, he was also a mbbs student in Sheikh Zayed medical college Lahore. The two of them shared a peculiar form of friendship, which looked bland, but went really deep. Sajeel told all about what happened to him, and what he planned to do, and as always Saiph was happy for him, that he found a track that’s unique to him and different from the world. 2 Hours went by, as they exchanged their blows of time one by one, and they decided to call it a day and hence ended the call. After that, Sajeel got up, took to his books, and his day just went by. Lights out time. And then sleep. Before going to bed, he felt that it might be his last one, the hunch every human as, ‘maybe tomorrow I won’t wake up’, the same was with Sajeel. But he did not give it much thought and went to sleep.

It was the next morning, he had overslept, not to the extent to miss his classes but he missed the time of the rising sun and his morning prayer as well. He got of his bed, felt boyish, unlike before, he felt young and energetic again, but these signs of youth also called for laziness. He changed into an ordinary jeans and a shirt, and went to his class. Just when he finally reached the room, he saw a familiar silhouette standing there. It was Sal. He looked serious, and stepped towards me, just said, “meet with me up later.” And passed by. Sajeel felt some chills. Something unpleasant might have happened. He looked ahead, to the path which led to section B and then looked at a class, and for some reason, he went to his own. His own classmates respected him, but none of them were technically in his group but that was his own fault, he just was not that social able and was happy that way too.

Today they were finally taken to the hospital tour. Something practical. Sajeel was interested, and that got his mind off from what had to come later. Time flew by and Sajeel apparently enjoyed a lot. “Dude you are a fun man, where were you hiding all that demeanor before?” One of his classmates asked him. He looked shocked but casually shrugged it off in a standard boyish form. So changes were starting to develop. He was accepting a newer vision of himself. They say, behind every successful man, there is a woman. This quote is rather taken to praise the feminine gender but Sajeel now understood that it was rather men who, due to the women changed to approach to be successful. Of course this version is a narrow minded concise approach applicable to only a few cases but Success has a flavor and life without femininity is flavorless, be it sweet or sour. Sajeel started enjoying himself in things that he did not before. Classes also came to an end with his realization of new things, which he was sure would continue, and today’s day had an optimistic approach on him. His worries were gone, and he headed towards section B. The class was empty, but Sal was there, outside the room, standing in a group of 3 boys. Seeing Sajeel, Sal said his byes, and the boys left. Sal came towards Sajeel and asked, “Do you know what I am going to ask you?” Sal was tall. Sajeel felt a bit intimidated but he was in a good mood, “Probably what happened yesterday?” “Yes, exactly.” His tone suddenly changed. It was the same old tone, the unseriousness and childishness of it felt relieving. “I felt so left out, so please, tell me what happened yesterday, I am very curious. It was a plain white roof. Sajeel tried to tilt his neck but found out he couldn’t. He couldn’t move a single muscle in his body. He tried to call out someone but there was no one, and neither was there a voice. He found out he couldn’t even speak. Tears kept rolling down his cheeks, slowly slowly, one by one. There was a clock in front of him, on the wall. Sajeel didn’t need to move here and there to see the time upon it. And he knew it was going to get busy soon. He just laid, expressionless. He was not happy. His heart felt dead.

Half an hour had passed and Sajeel already got his first visitor. But strangely it was Saiph. And not his parents. He felt a real genuine heart beat seeing that face. But … He looked older. Already a man. Wearing the white coat that Sajeel too was supposed to wear. Regardless of the age factor that dawned upon him a terror which he closed in his subconscious for now, for he just wanted to feel happiness. He wanted to stand alive again. Kaila, that means she was still there, worried for her… wai…t…in… for her…. At night, Sajeel, was having troubles with his sleeps, the fear of his eyes yet not opening up again if he slept. We often feel that right, we might not make it to the morning, but it’s a big problem when that feeling condenses into a fear, yes feelings and fear are far different. Feelings envelop the heart from the inside making their way out, where as fears, make their way from the outside, eating their way to the core, gripping your very foundations in its palm. Its torture, and trauma is the bond that sticks the fear to the hearts. Sajeel’s trauma was still very fresh. Staring up, still unable to move, he cried. The flowing tears made him feel as if he still could move, and that was a ray of hope. How artistic of humans, finding hope in even their weakness. As long as there is even the smallest of things below us we feel in power. Its strength they say, but is it? Its a weakness, cause it’s a mirage of your uphold in life. People often look at the top most of the leader board. But the real key to success is neither the top, nor the bottom. It is the thing right above you and the one right below you. That is the real elevator that rises slowly slowly to a proper stability.

Something struck him, his prayers…. 15 years of prayers… but wait, religion pardons it right. I had a logical reason, Sajeel thought, and it flashed his mind, all those prayers he missed on purpose in the last weeks before his accident. He felt really guilty to even ask help from his creator. He must be watching, he knows, if he really wants to help me he will, he will…. Sajeel was counselling himself…. He did not pray, rather he tried to speak up. It was a futile attempt. But in just 5 minutes of trying, he heard a slight faint whisper from his own mouths. To an observer, he was just moving his lips, but there was a voice, he could hear it. K..a..i..l..a… Kai..la… Kaila… he kept repeating. Why? Why was the name of the girl who he never really got close to on his lips? They never got close, yet got closer than the relationship a man enjoys with his creator, why? Humans are love craving creatures. If they fall in love, they go crazy, but if they realize it is not love, they force it upon themselves. They HAVE to instead of doing it. And amazingly this works. This formula worked for Sajeel. Who wouldn’t say he is not in love. But, just like the underworld and the seventh star are both divine realms for gods, love is also a realm for human, yes, love, that wings you to sky, and love that sticks you down deeper and deeper into the emotions. Underworld is not necessarily a bad place; it’s made for bad people. Same like that is the case with love, it is not bad, it’s just.., humans fail to find out the correct form for themselves. They think there is just love that they forget the duality of reality.

He kept saying Kaila, slowly, whispering it to his own lips, the sound getting louder bit by bit. It was no longer just a name of his beloved, it was more like a spell he was charting up, to hallucinate himself maybe, to sleep, to sleep.

Sajeel’s eyes opened, he was still feeling stiff. He saw there was no one else in the room, and just closed his eyes back. Though he did not sleep again, he did go into a slumber like state where he kept imagining how things would have been, had this accident not occurred. Imagining the not happened is ecstatic because the one who is imagining things wanted for those thoughts to come real, that means he had an idea of the feelings that might follow those experiences and imagining them gives them the gist of those emotions, like a demo version for a game. Sajeel was also just cooling down his lost years. For some reason he felt a bit calmer then yesterday. The door opened, the unslept Sajeel felt that and opened his eyes. It was Saiph. Sajeel gave him a smile. “Hey” Sajeel said, as Saiph stopped in his tracks to hear his voice. Sajeel himself hadn’t noticed that he spoke aloud but Saiph’s excitement made him aware that something happened, and he realized it after a second or two and, couldn’t help but giggle which was a bit too early from him resulting him to have a cough fit but Saiph came and lifted his head up and it got better. Saiph was genuinely happy, and said, “Your rehabilitation starts today Sajeel, we are gonna get you up in no time.” Sajeel smiled as to show him he was ready but at the same time his smile asked him something reminding him of the unfinished talk they had yesterday. Saiph looked at him and said, I would tell you slowly slowly everything if you did good in your rehab. A reward system, hahaha Sajeel laughed in his mind to the thought, it was not a bad idea. He had decided he would keep a hopeful approach to things.

Physiotherapists, counsellors and what not started working on Sajeel’s body. Sajeel too gave his best, and did his all he could. It was a really strenuous task. One almost feels like giving midway and that it might not be possible, but even a normal person thinks that way on as small as a scoring good on his exam task, so a guy who has been in a coma for 15 years has every right to think it’s impossible. The real thing is to not bring these thoughts to reality. We often think how good it might be if that happens or this happens, but does it happen? Not mostly, so in times which feels impossible, just take your revenge from life by not making the impossible come true. It’s just your though like the good feelings you had, they didn’t bear fruit right, we won’t let this impossibleness bear fruit either. That’s how his counsellor motivated Sajeel, who did his best to stick to his goals.

More than 2 months had passed. His different class fellows had come to meet him for the formalities, all had started their families. So many reunions with other relatives. All this made Sajeel feel quite hopeful. So many people were paying their regards. Even if you know something is being done as a formality, doesn’t mean you don’t enjoy it. Sajeel had developed the notion that it was like being served your favorite drink or dish as a formality, you would eat it, and enjoy the substance rather than the reason, so why not enjoy the care, even if it was just superficial, at least it made you feel good. By now Sajeel was able to start walking with the help of crutches and supports. He could sit perfectly fine. And his next task was to walk properly on his own feet. His voice was totally back. His weak body regaining the lost mass and becoming healthier than before. To his achievements Saiph said, as a reward, today I will let you meet a special pair. Sajeel wondered who it was. A muscular man came forward, with a smirk on his face that could belong to only one person, Sajeel didn’t even need to stress his memory. He was in the lawn of the hospital, on a wheelchair with Saiph at his back, Seeing Sal, Sajeel, with an effort got up wobbly but managed to do it on his own and hugged an old friend. Salman was really happy seeing the man stand to his feet, haven’t our boy grown now haha he said. Sajeel sat back on his chair and Salman stepped aside and that’s when the shock dawned upon him, the girl who stood their supposedly to be Mrs. Salman, was no other than Mahnoor. Sajeel seeing that laughed a lot, it was after so long that Sajeel had laughed in such a free manner, he felt really good. Still unable to control his laugh, Sajeel said, “Hahaha what did you find in this black sheep that you married him hahah” “well I though in world filled with white wool, black wool would sell better for being unique so I thought it was a profitable deal, haha” Mahnoor said, which referred to Sal as being a unique kind man, a sort of a compliment hidden in sarcasm, to which all 4 of them laughed. Sal’s position still hadn’t changed. Sajeel for once felt really happy, and his eyes got teary, “I’m so happy for you guys, and so happy you came.” Sal jocked down on his knees to come face to face with Sal, “We were, at least I was there with you mate, don’t worry, we are waiting for you to get back up, so once again, let us all meet at the IGLOO ice cream’s, I hope they haven’t closed that down, so hurry, all 4 of us are in wait for you.” All 4. He has said it in a way that had excluded of Sajeel, there 3 other only present by then, that could only mean she was still here. Then why hadn’t she come yet? Sajeel quenched his theories and questions for a halt, and took a deep breath with his eyes closed. He opened them and gave Sal a smile showing that yes, he will, he himself was waiting for their get together.

The thought was new, rather it was the first one that struck Sajeel when he started thinking on all of the situation. He looked back at his memories and remember seeing Kaila among the three faces that were above him before his eyes closed down. Was it really Kaila? Did he saved her, was she actually struck of the danger? What if, … if she is no longer with us, and they were all just keeping it in a way to keep me away from a nervous breakdown. Despite thinking all this with the calmest and coolest of heads, the thought alone shook Sajeel’s body with fear, and he dared not think further. It was his unconscious that made him ask this question and then answer it as well as if to prepare him for the worst case scenario.

“Hey, Saiph. Honestly tell me. Kaila is alive right? I did save her right? Tell me my 15 years were not in vain. Tell me I can be with her.” Sajeel has asked Saiph directly. It was around the time when Sajeel started walking on his own. His movements were not normal. But this meant that his rehab was going to end in another one month. After a deep breath, with a sad face Saiph turned to Sajeel. Sajeel’s parents were also in the room, but they just kept silent. It appears they were made aware of who Kaila was. And what she meant. “Look Sajeel, she’s alive. I assure you. She’s waiting for you.” Saiph answered to the best of keeping the situation cool. “And she hasn’t married someone right?” Saiph looked at Sajeel, “Why would you ask me this question?” “Why, can’t I?” Sajeel met Saiph’s question with a surprise. “No, she hasn’t married someone.” Saiph stoically replied to Sajeel. There were so many thigs, that the harsh reality was going to throw up against Sajeel. Sajeel knew this, lost 15 years are not easy to cope up with. This hospital and rehab sort of acted as a shield, a sanctuary which he had to leave sooner or later, and that later was approaching. Though, if his top most priority was secured, he was confident he would fight all else.

The following month passed as well. He met Sal and Mahnoor twice again. He was starting to show the matureness one would expect of a 36-year-old man. One would not be able to guess this man spent 15 years in sleep. And he finally was able to walk properly, his health restored. His time to finally step outside was here. And he went to Saiph, who was so happy to see his best friend finally walking towards him dressed up, on his own. Saiph felt proud. Sajeel stood to him and said, Saiph, the day has come, it’s time for my reward. Saiph smiled and said, “Yeah, let’s go meet her.” And they both drove off.

“That’s a nice car you have their, Civic surely upgraded their game while I slept.” Saiph smiled to his innocent compliment. It was the walled city they were in. Lahore. They drove off for quite some while. Until they finally entered gates, Bahria Town. As soon as they entered the gates, Sajeel started feeling the pressure. His chest got tight. Saiph had a bit of a sad face seeing Sajeel getting restless. Was it okay to meet like this? Is it natural, does she know I am coming? And so many question just kept followed his mind, how should I react? How would she react? Does she have feelings for me still? Sajeel started to feel scared. “Hey Saiph, let’s go back. I don’t think im ready yet suddenly to face her.” Saiph was driving on, he gave Sajeel a glance, “I knew you would say that, that is why I …” He stopped the car in front of a beautiful lush house. Sajeel saw the name plate in front of the house, ‘Dr. Saiph-ur-Rehman.’ Sajeel let out a laughter, “Hahaha, best friends are such clever creatures, they know what’s going on, well its good you didn’t disclose it to me before that we would be going to your house. Whew. I need time after all to meet Kaila, you guys have made it such a suspense situation that it’s getting harder for me haha…” Sajeel got out of the car. Saiph got out as well. He looked at the main gate, as they heard the door from inside being opened. Someone from the lounge was coming to open the main gate. Saiph stood by the car’s gate. And Sajeel by the main gate, as it opened. Life is cruel. We all know that. By now many would have already seen how the game of chess played by life leads to tragedy when someone gets marked. Kaila stood there. And Sajeel just …. Long hair, more beautiful than before, Sajeel stood there, unable to process the thing that had just came to term with him. He looked at the name plate outside the house again. Then at the main gate where she stood. He turned back to see Saiph, who just lowered his head. “Sajeel.” Kaila said in the voice which literally shook Sajeel’s internals from the inside, hurricanes originated all at once, wreaking havoc everywhere. He started shivering and tears got to his eyes… “Sajeel, look at me, I know how this might feel but believe me, hear us out first..” Sajeel glared at Kaila as if only to induce more self-damage. He looked again at Saiph, “Why, Why Karagami, Why, you said she wasn’t married to someone?” “Is Saiph someone, Sajeel. The voice behind him spoke up. Wasn’t he your other half. Weren’t you the one who said he was, huh, Sajeel. Tell me, did you think emotionally blaming both of us into a corner is fair.” Her voice wobbled. It showed that she was crying as well. Sajeel whose face was turned to Saiph had no courage to turn back on those words. “I waited so much for you, prayed so much. I really loved you I had realized, I wanted to be with you, but Sajeel, tell me, you wouldn’t wake up, no matter how many times I would caress your hair, or weep to ask you to get back. You won’t Sajeel, you did not. And the one who supported me the most was this guy who you are looking at with eyes as if he was the culprit. He was the one who kept me from breaking, and he loved you as well, and I couldn’t help but see your image in him.” By now Sajeel turned back to Kaila, she had clenched her fist by her chest, as if she was forcing the words out of her. Her eyes, all teared and red, revealing dark spots under her eyes. “Sajeel, I was the one, it was me who confessed Saiph. He denied you know, but at the end, we had no option, such is life, we moved on, we had too, it was hard for us as well, we waited more than 10 years…. I couldn’t do my Mbbs as well, I just couldn’t. Sajeel, will you still hate him, because if you do, you have to hate me first.” The strength from Sajeel’s leg gave way, and his emotions got the best of him, the turmoil he was in which was not explainable to even him at that point, once again, his eyes blacked out, he gave up. He had given up. He did not want to live no more.

It was the waiting area. Sajeel’s mother was crying while using his father’s shoulder as a support. Saiph and Kaila were sitting. The doctor came out. “He has had a ‘nervous breakdown’ we tried everything we could do, his pulse kept falling, we even had to shock him but it appeared that he himself had no will left. It appears the emotional trauma he just faced was too enormous for him to bear. I am sorry to say but he won’t make it out back as a healthy person, and has a high chance of suffering from a psychological problem from here on out. Please execute extra care in his nursing, he is in a delicate situation.” All 4 of them hearing the daughter just crashed down, everyone feeling the guilt. How did it all came to this. And most of all Why? But, there was not much that could be done. Harsh realities struck every now and then, some of them just get struck more, those lucky ones should thank God and live on, those being struck by the cruelty should just accept it their fate and move on to the best of their limit. Nothing much can be done.

Time went by, Sajeel woke up the very next day. Back to hospital in just one day. Wait, the same day he left it, not even one day, Ha, how ironic. He did not saw Kaila, maybe she had not the guts to face him. She was a coward despite portraying a strong character. Saiph did come but Sajeel didn’t eve looked him in the eye and did not replied anything to what he said. That was last he saw of him for quite some while then. The only one who regularly looked after him were his own parents. Sajeel would often stare into the nothing. His parents often wondered what he might be thinking and were worried for him but did not question it much. Sajeel would answer to normal question normally, it appeared he still was in control of his consciousness, he just seemed to have gone tyrant to the notion of life and god itself. ‘God’. Was it because he left his prayers in his pursuit of a worldly love that he was struck with this misfortune. Would someone as sovereign as God really do that… Haha who am I kidding, who am I thinking to blame, I can’t blame anyone, only myself. Haha, maybe I should have let Kaila get hit back then. This way she might has gone into the coma haha and I would have waited for her. All would have been good haha. That means I’m the idiot one haha, hahhaah.

With silly thoughts like that, Sajeel would always fill his head. It had been one whole week now. He was again discharged from the hospital. This time he went to his parents’ home. His own home. He spent the first 3 days silent, mostly coiled up in his own bed. His parents were constantly afraid of him ending up doing something irrational. Maybe there were right, but they did not impose any restrictions because they were afraid that might backfire as well. Situation where you meet disasters at both ends are quite hardy to overcome right, what should be done? Nothing. The disasters are probably not for overcoming, because they are the stimulus to move things forward. Sometimes that’s the way life chooses. Acceptance is what can reduce the impact on to the fragile human soul and body.

It was the fifth morning, when Sajeel’s mother got up for the fajr prayer, and though she should ask Sajeel to offer as well, for it might make him feel better. But to her surprise, Sajeel was already offering. She was astonished and so happy that she closed the door of the room back. 2 hours later when she got up again, to ready the breakfast, she called up on him but got no reply. She went to check on him. But, he was not there. His room was arranged. And no signs of someone being there. Any mother would panic to this sight, she called Sajeel’s father and Saiph as well because he was one of the few other people she could reply on. They both got onto finding him. What they did not realized was, there was only one place that he would go to.

He rang the bell of the same house which he once called beautiful, but it now seemed as if it would fall on him any moment. The door opened, Kaila, on the phone with someone suddenly seeing Sajeel, hanged up the call. “Kaila, I thought a lot on it. We can still be together.” Sajeel spoke in a very calm and cool manner. Kaila on the other hand got red and furious, “have you no shame Sajeel?” she made a face that showed her disgust at Sajeel. “Look, I know if I ask Saiph he would understand, then we can marry after he leaves you…” Kaila almost slapped Sajeel but stopped midway. She again started to cry, tears mixed, of despair, anger, regret and so on. “Please Sajeel, just leave me, please I beg you, I have a 2-year-old inside of the house. Don’t ask the impossible, stop making more difficulties for all of us.” It was now as if she was begging, her voice really low and wobbly. “I have planned to talk to Saiph today.” Sajeel said in the same lifeless manner once again. Kaila looked at him and suddenly bloated up all her storm of emotion s into a scream, “GET OUUUUUT, JUST GOOOOO, GEETTTTT OUTTTTT, GOOOOO….” She literally started screaming to which Sajeel held her by her shoulders, “WHY, WHY Kaila, why… when you love me why are you forcing yourself, why won’t you choooose me WHY. …” Sajeel had lost his composure and was shaking again and his eyes so strange by the insecurity, he seemed as if he would break if Kaila backed of from him. “I cannot” Kaila said, I just cannot, she sobbed as she said, “Im happy Sajeel, I am happy, please leave, don’t come back… please ….” “I will do anything Kaila, anything, if you cannot leave him, I can become something, just please don’t reject me, just tell me what do I have to doooo….” Sajeel had almost turned into a maniac as he was saying this, shaking Kaila as if just wanting her acceptance, “Pleaaaaaseeee tell me, anything, I would do anything, be anything….” “JUST GET LOST, PLEASE …. DON’T HURT ME ANYMORE….” Kaila dropped to her knees as she said that. Sajeel who stood solely on her support lost it. He fell down as well. Kaila got up, wiped her tears, though she could not stop those tears and hiccups, she closed the door on him. He could hear her crying once again though while she entered back inside the house. What was it, that he heard then, for some strange reason he could heard birds. Pigeons, parrots, sparrows, he looked up, from the slit between the gate, there was a big cage in the garage, He noticed it right now, there were birds and birds. He got up and started a broken laughter and dallied his way away from there.

7 years had passed. There was no sign of Sajeel. His parents had given up. Saiph could not find him anywhere as well. No one knew where he was, and was proposed dead. Time diluted everyone’s feelings and things started to go well because the man marked by life had been removed for the chess board, it was like check mate for this case. The game was over, but one last move was still left.

It was a forests, mountains as well, and among the mountains, there was a cave. Sajeel, in tattered clothes, and a really messy situation, was surrounded by many birds. He would toil here and there on the ground, making voices as if mimicking the birds. The birds themselves didn’t mind it as well. At night he would cry and cry to ask to be reborn as a bird, all he knew was that he needed to be a bird. He needed to meet someone, fly to their arms with his wings opened, snuggle his beak with their body so feel their bodily warmth. He had forgotten all else. He had gone berserk and haywire as ordinary people would say, artist might say he has opened up gates to a new art, poets and writers might say he has attained the 13th and final stage of love. But in reality all he had done was go crazy all on his own. In his attempt to be a bird which was impossible, he brought the impossible come to life by making it a reality. If all the misfortune can be a reality, then surely the impossible in his favor can be a reality as well.

To him, he was a bird. He had finally attainted the one form where he was sure he would be accepted by that someone. He would look at his hands and he saw wings, he touched his nose and he felt the cartilaginous beak, and he headed out. Chirping or his so called chirping for in reality he was just screaming like a person who has no know how of anything. He kept jumping and skipping as it made him feel he was gliding. Where was he going. He knew nothing, he just kept on going…. Eventually leading on to a bridge. He grabbed the fence of the bridge as if sitting on it with its claws. It was time for his flight, to meet the one he had fallen in love with. And he flew, he flew as he falls down. He felt the air rushing his body, as if lifting himself to his destination. He had finally done it. The real source of love, he had attainted it. The love which arose from the self and generated equally to the outside. It was not directed to just one someone, Sajeel was flying, through planes that made him devoid of the physical plane, it was time for him to leave the physical and join the trance which he first experienced and become an eternal part of it. In the grasp of his creator, who created him, and brought all that he had gone through, yet still chose only him to be worthy of feeling the real love, the love that made him fly, the Birds Love.

THE END
